text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Gate auto-apply on a semantic diff test that runs only against edited files. This keeps the system safe by verifying changes don’t break existing behavior while avoiding the cost of full-project regression checks. The trade-off is that edits might still introduce bugs in untested parts of the codebase, but that risk is lower than the overhead of running full tests on every change.

name: Gauge
text: The semantic diff test only catches changes that break *tested* behavior—it won’t flag edits that subtly alter untested logic or introduce new bugs in untouched files. A better alternative is to run a *targeted* regression suite on the edited files’ dependencies, not just the files themselves. Settle it by proving the regression suite catches the edge cases the semantic diff misses.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Run the semantic diff test against *all* edited files *and* their direct dependencies. This catches regressions where a change in one file breaks another file that depends on it, without paying the full-project regression cost. The trade-off is that we still miss bugs that propagate through indirect dependencies or untested code paths.

name: Gauge
text: The targeted regression suite still misses bugs that propagate through indirect dependencies—changes ripple outward unpredictably. A better alternative is to run a *minimal* full-project regression suite *only when* the semantic diff flags a high-risk edit (e.g., core logic or API changes). Settle by measuring the false-negative rate of the targeted suite against real regressions in the last 6 months.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Gate auto-apply on two checks—first, a semantic diff against all edited files and their direct dependencies; second, a minimal full-project regression suite triggered only for high-risk edits (core logic or API changes).

Result must deliver: A working auto-apply system that blocks unsafe changes while keeping runtime costs low. Owner: Sprocket.
